tasks.title: Create PromptFrontmatterParser using YamlDotNet
tasks.description: Implement a small parser that reads the frontmatter block out of a .prompt file's raw text and produces a (PromptFrontmatter, Body) tuple. Partial frontmatter (e.g. only `name:`) tolerates missing fields with the same defaults
Malformed YAML throws an exception that identifies the file key
Implementation uses YamlDotNet (already in Directory.Packages.props) and lives under Prompts/Infrastructure/

tasks.title: Create PromptTemplateEngine (render + extract)
tasks.description: Implement the server-side render engine as a pure C# port of runner renderTemplate semantics, with the differences spelled out in the spec: 5-pass cap, missing variables left in place AND recorded in a list, non-string values JSON-stringified. Also expose a static ExtractVariables(body) that does a regex scan (no rendering) returning a sorted, deduplicated list of paths.
acceptanceCriteria: Render(body, variables) returns (rendered, missingVariables, depth) where rendered is the body with ${{ path }} tokens expanded up to 5 passes, missingVariables is the deduplicated sorted list of unresolvable paths, and depth is the number of passes that produced a change
Missing variable leaves the literal `${{ path }}` token in rendered and records the path in missingVariables
Non-string values (object, array, number, boolean) are JSON-stringified; null becomes the literal string `null`
A cyclic/never-converging input does not loop (5 passes, then returns the last state with whatever `${{ ... }}` remain)
ExtractVariables(body) returns the sorted unique list of paths appearing in `${{ ... }}` markers, without performing any rendering
Engine is registered as a singleton in DI (stateless)

ExtractVariables test verifies sorted, deduplicated output for duplicate and out-of-order references

tasks.title: Validate prompts.* keys in start-work; return 400 missing_prompts
tasks.description: In IssueGrain.StartWorkAsync, after computing the merged prompts dictionary and before calling wfGrain.StartAsync, scan the workflow definition for `${{ prompts.<key> }}` references and throw a specific MissingPromptsException listing the missing keys. (The ordering matters: MissingPromptsException inherits from InvalidOperationException, so the dedicated catch must run first.)
